e-4394.worked_solution:

e-4395.problem:
Which of the following matrices are lower triangular matrices?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14075464/assets/ad9636de9b8c93338350a6b99d88476b481ed1bf03a5dd64935abedbdb626524.png)
e-4395.worked_solution:
The matrix $B$ is a lower triangular matrix since all the entries above the main diagonal are zeros.

The matrices $A$ and $C$ are *not* lower triangular matrices since they each have a non-zero element above the main diagonal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{23} & =1\ne 0 \\ {c}_{13} & =1\ne 0\end{aligned}
$$

e-4498.knowledge_point: Identifying Correct Statements About a Matrix
e-4498.problem:
Consider the matrix 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14075464/assets/4dd9b1c1b3d789c166ecd8f6d2a909609c7f4324705c84115cce84a29181bf32.png)
Which of the following statements are true?

- $A$ is upper triangular

- $A$ is lower triangular

- $A^T-A$ is lower triangular
e-4498.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false, since $A$ has non-zero entries below the main diagonal:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14075464/assets/c1ec838cd30cca8fbb2e3996d5a7d84dadb233e1951d05b532a9d606d887eb2f.png)

- Statement II is true, since all the entries above the main diagonal are zeros:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14075464/assets/f39c68a9b1f5e16caffbf159b629a958e147e14099334b049bdfcd857eef84d2.png)

- Statement III is false, since the result of $A^T-A$ has non-zero entries above the main diagonal:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14075464/assets/f4415c87201f5b92f23e3320c313cd58ac4e720135928645896f976614c5eaa0.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".

decision.explanation: A is upper triangular because all three entries below its main diagonal are zero. Each other choice has a nonzero entry below the main diagonal.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: Which of the following is an upper triangular matrix?
after.worked_solution:
Notice that $A$ is a matrix for which all entries *below* the diagonal are $0$'s:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Hence, it is an upper triangular matrix. 

By contrast, matrices $B$, $C$, $D$, and $E$ each have at least one non-zero entry below the diagonal:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -5 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,E=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

So, they are not upper triangular matrices.

Question 6

Which of the following is an upper triangular matrix?

a
A=[010023000]
b
E=[1011]
c
C=[010−1230−30]
d
D=[1111]
e
B=[200020−500]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that A is a matrix for which all entries below the diagonal are 0's: A=[010023000] Hence, it is an upper triangular matrix.

By contrast, matrices B, C, D, and E each have at least one non-zero entry below the diagonal:

B=[200020−500],C=[010−1230−30],D=[1111],E=[1011].

So, they are not upper triangular matrices.

content.problem: Which of the following is an upper triangular matrix?
content.worked_solution:
Notice that $A$ is a matrix for which all entries *below* the diagonal are $0$'s:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Hence, it is an upper triangular matrix. 

By contrast, matrices $B$, $C$, $D$, and $E$ each have at least one non-zero entry below the diagonal:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -5 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,E=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

So, they are not upper triangular matrices.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: Which of the following is a lower triangular matrix?
after.worked_solution:
Notice that $B$ is a matrix for which all entries *above* the diagonal are $0$'s:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Hence, it is a lower triangular matrix. 

By contrast, matrices $A$, $C$, $D$, and $E$ each have at least one non-zero entry above the diagonal:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,E=[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & -7 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, they are not lower triangular matrices.

content.worked_solution:
Notice that $B$ is a matrix for which all entries *above* the diagonal are $0$'s:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Hence, it is a lower triangular matrix. 

By contrast, matrices $A$, $C$, $D$, and $E$ each have at least one non-zero entry above the diagonal:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,E=[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & -7 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, they are not lower triangular matrices.

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]

$$

$$
